title: What the auditors wrote about the City’s accounts, year by year
question: Did the outside auditor sign off on the City’s accounts and its use of federal grants each year, and how many problems did it report?
finding: The auditor gave a clean opinion on the City’s accounts in all 11 years from fiscal 2015 to 2025. The yearly audit reports list 11 findings over the period, 4 on the accounts and 7 on grants; 2 were rated a material weakness, the most serious grade. 6 years had no finding at all (2017, 2019, 2021, 2022, 2024, 2025). The opinion on the use of federal grants was not clean once, in fiscal 2020 (qualified for one programme: Disaster Grants – Public Assistance (Presidentially Declared Disasters)). The accounts were signed off between 141 days (fiscal 2016) and 268 days (fiscal 2018) after the year closed.
how: From the text of each year’s annual financial report: the independent auditor’s letter (the wording of the opinion, the date beside the signature, and the first sentence of any “emphasis of matter” paragraph). From each year’s single audit of federal grants: the labelled lines of “Section I, Summary of Auditor’s Results” and every finding numbered for that year in the schedule that follows. A finding is a repeat when the same report says last year’s finding under the same heading had not been fixed, or says so in the finding itself. Page numbers are pages of the file.
limits: A clean opinion says the accounts are fairly stated; it is not a check on whether money was well spent, and the grant audit tests only the federal programmes each report lists as “major” for that year. Findings are counted from the report text by pattern, so each row links to the page to check. An “emphasis of matter” paragraph draws attention to something already in the accounts, often a new accounting rule, and is not a criticism. A later signing date can have several causes: the slowest year, fiscal 2018, was the first under a new City financial system brought in on July 3, 2017, which that year’s finding describes. The fiscal 2020 single audit answers “No” to whether any federal-grant findings had to be reported, yet its schedule lists finding 2020-002; the summary line looks wrong, and the finding is counted here.
